historical_record.description: Western Addition Branch Library, designed by Appleton & Wolfard.
The library was built in Hamilton Square.
The Western Addition Branch Library was renovated early in the year, losing enough of its original fabric that it was judged ineligible for landmark status; its once-exposed brick has been painted.
The Western Addition Library marked its 25th anniversary on December 14, 1991, when a new collection on African and African-American history and culture was unveiled.
The Art Commission approved the Phase 3 drawings for the Western Addition Branch Library by Appleton & Wolfard.

Kent Ford of the Department of Public Works' Bureau of Architecture presented his design for a $2.4 million renovation of the 1965 Appleton and Wolfard building, with seismic and accessibility work and about 250 square feet more space.
The Recreation and Park Commission agreed to give the Library Commission land at the west end of Hamilton Playground for a Western Addition branch library.
The Library Commission named Appleton & Wolfard project architects for the Western Addition branch library, as well as for the new Excelsior branch.
The Library Commission approved the final plans for the Western Addition Branch Library, essentially the design it had approved at the preliminary stage.
The Western Addition Branch Library opened for service that summer; its formal dedication was scheduled for September 21, 1966.
The Library Commission was shown the collages that Betty Burley designed and made for the wall of the children's room at the Western Addition Branch Library.
